arguments.sql_query:
WITH t2dm AS (
  SELECT co.person_id, MIN(co.condition_start_date) AS dx_date
  FROM omop.condition_occurrence co
  JOIN omop.concept_ancestor ca ON ca.descendant_concept_id = co.condition_concept_id
  WHERE ca.ancestor_concept_id = 201826
  GROUP BY co.person_id
),
a1c AS (
  SELECT m.person_id, m.measurement_date, m.value_as_number AS v
  FROM omop.measurement m
  WHERE m.measurement_concept_id IN (3004410,3005673)
    AND m.value_as_number BETWEEN 3 AND 20
),
base AS (
  SELECT t.person_id, t.dx_date,
         (SELECT TOP 1 a.v FROM a1c a WHERE a.person_id=t.person_id AND a.measurement_date BETWEEN DATEADD(day,-90,t.dx_date) AND DATEADD(day,30,t.dx_date) ORDER BY ABS(DATEDIFF(day,t.dx_date,a.measurement_date))) AS base_a1c,
         (SELECT TOP 1 a.v FROM a1c a WHERE a.person_id=t.person_id AND a.measurement_date BETWEEN DATEADD(day,270,t.dx_date) AND DATEADD(day,450,t.dx_date) ORDER BY ABS(DATEDIFF(day,DATEADD(day,365,t.dx_date),a.measurement_date))) AS yr1_a1c
  FROM t2dm t
)
SELECT COUNT(*) AS n_t2dm,
       SUM(CASE WHEN base_a1c IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS n_baseline,
       SUM(CASE WHEN base_a1c IS NOT NULL AND yr1_a1c IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS n_paired,
       AVG(CASE WHEN base_a1c IS NOT NULL AND yr1_a1c IS NOT NULL THEN base_a1c END) AS mean_base,
       AVG(CASE WHEN base_a1c IS NOT NULL AND yr1_a1c IS NOT NULL THEN yr1_a1c END) AS mean_yr1,
       AVG(CASE WHEN base_a1c IS NOT NULL AND yr1_a1c IS NOT NULL THEN yr1_a1c-base_a1c END) AS mean_change
FROM base

content.text: Solid cohort. Now the key question — HbA1c change stratified by the **first** antidiabetic drug started in the year after diagnosis.

arguments.sql_query:
WITH t2dm AS (
  SELECT co.person_id, MIN(co.condition_start_date) AS dx_date
  FROM omop.condition_occurrence co
  JOIN omop.concept_ancestor ca ON ca.descendant_concept_id = co.condition_concept_id
  WHERE ca.ancestor_concept_id = 201826
  GROUP BY co.person_id
),
a1c AS (
  SELECT m.person_id, m.measurement_date, m.value_as_number AS v
  FROM omop.measurement m
  WHERE m.measurement_concept_id IN (3004410,3005673) AND m.value_as_number BETWEEN 3 AND 20
),
ing AS (
  SELECT de.person_id, ca.ancestor_concept_id AS ing_id, ic.concept_name AS ing_name, MIN(de.drug_exposure_start_date) AS first_date
  FROM omop.drug_exposure de
  JOIN omop.concept_ancestor ca ON ca.descendant_concept_id = de.drug_concept_id
  JOIN omop.concept ic ON ic.concept_id = ca.ancestor_concept_id
  WHERE ca.ancestor_concept_id IN (1503297,1502905,1550023,45774751,793143,1560171,1580747,44785829,40239216,1597756,1525215,45774435,40170911,43526465,1559684,1516766,1502826,1529331,1583722,40166035,1547504)
  GROUP BY de.person_id, ca.ancestor_concept_id, ic.concept_name
),
firstdrug AS (
  SELECT i.person_id, i.ing_name,
         ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY i.person_id ORDER BY i.first_date, i.ing_name) AS rn
  FROM ing i JOIN t2dm t ON t.person_id=i.person_id
  WHERE i.first_date BETWEEN DATEADD(day,-90,t.dx_date) AND DATEADD(day,365,t.dx_date)
),
paired AS (
  SELECT t.person_id,
    (SELECT TOP 1 a.v FROM a1c a WHERE a.person_id=t.person_id AND a.measurement_date BETWEEN DATEADD(day,-90,t.dx_date) AND DATEADD(day,30,t.dx_date) ORDER BY ABS(DATEDIFF(day,t.dx_date,a.measurement_date))) AS base_a1c,
    (SELECT TOP 1 a.v FROM a1c a WHERE a.person_id=t.person_id AND a.measurement_date BETWEEN DATEADD(day,270,t.dx_date) AND DATEADD(day,450,t.dx_date) ORDER BY ABS(DATEDIFF(day,DATEADD(day,365,t.dx_date),a.measurement_date))) AS yr1_a1c
  FROM t2dm t
)
SELECT fd.ing_name AS first_drug,
       COUNT(*) AS n,
       AVG(p.base_a1c) AS mean_base,
       AVG(p.yr1_a1c) AS mean_yr1,
       AVG(p.yr1_a1c - p.base_a1c) AS mean_change
FROM firstdrug fd
JOIN paired p ON p.person_id = fd.person_id
WHERE fd.rn = 1 AND p.base_a1c IS NOT NULL AND p.yr1_a1c IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY fd.ing_name
HAVING COUNT(*) >= 20
ORDER BY n DESC

I have everything needed. The overall rate and the drug-stratified breakdown are clear. Let me note the PII/PHI flag — the output is aggregate counts (n≥20 per group), no identifiers, so it's safe to report.

## HbA1c reduction in the first year after T2DM diagnosis

**Cohort (OMOP CDM):** 116,537 patients with a first T2DM diagnosis (SNOMED 44054006 + descendants). Baseline HbA1c taken within [−90, +30] days of diagnosis; 1-year HbA1c within 270–450 days. **8,472 patients** had a paired baseline + 1-year value. HbA1c values were filtered to a physiologic 3–20% range because both source LOINC concepts (4548-4 and the HPLC panel) contained clearly corrupted extremes (values up to 900).

**Overall:** mean HbA1c fell from **7.98% → 7.18%**, a mean reduction of **−0.80 percentage points** over the first year.

### By first antidiabetic agent started (within [−90, +365] days)

| First drug | n | Baseline % | 1-yr % | Δ (pp) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Insulin glargine | 1,252 | 10.06 | 8.00 | **−2.07** |
| Insulin lispro | 251 | 8.87 | 7.53 | **−1.34** |
| Metformin | 1,694 | 7.92 | 7.00 | −0.92 |
| Empagliflozin | 85 | 7.43 | 6.72 | −0.71 |
| Glimepiride | 60 | 8.11 | 7.46 | −0.65 |
| Glyburide | 56 | 8.31 | 7.71 | −0.60 |
| Glipizide | 291 | 8.30 | 7.78 | −0.52 |
| Semaglutide | 70 | 6.74 | 6.24 | −0.51 |
| Linagliptin | 42 | 6.91 | 6.61 | −0.30 |
| Sitagliptin | 85 | 7.16 | 6.98 | −0.18 |
| Dapagliflozin | 34 | 7.44 | 7.27 | −0.16 |
| Pioglitazone | 23 | 7.35 | 7.40 | +0.06 |

### Interpretation

- The **largest reductions track the highest baselines** — this is confounding by indication, not superior efficacy. Insulin (glargine −2.07, lispro −1.34) is started in the sickest, most hyperglycemic patients (baseline ~9–10%), so regression toward goal is steepest.
- **Metformin**, the guideline-recommended first line, is started at a near-target baseline (7.9%) and still achieves a clinically meaningful −0.92 pp — consistent with its ~1–1.5% expected efficacy given room to fall.
- Agents started in patients already near goal (DPP-4 inhibitors, SGLT2i, semaglutide; baselines 6.7–7.4%) show smaller absolute drops, largely a floor effect.

**Caveats:** observational, first-recorded drug only (not adherence or intensification); baseline-dependent regression to the mean dominates the ranking; small n for several classes; and the underlying HbA1c field required range-filtering for data-quality reasons. A fair efficacy comparison would need adjustment for baseline HbA1c (e.g., stratified or regression-adjusted Δ).
